Description: [General] eNOAD dysfunctional/critical equipment reporting (33 CFR 164) — All defective machinery must be reported to USCG via eNOA; revised eNOA without delay if found after submission. M/E and G/E normal operation confirmed before US call (USCG focus area; USD 150K fine imposed on a managed vessel in 2024). Deviation letter required via local agent.

[General] Garbage handling (CBP penalty) — Garbage must be kept in tight, covered, leak-proof receptacles per 33 CFR 94.5. Avoid large bags; if unavoidable, keep tied in deck store and plan discharge at upcoming ports.
[General] HAZMAT CBT training — Vessels calling USA require IMDG CBT (No.0053 Basic / No.0151 Advanced) for all crew, 3-year interval, printed records kept onboard.

[General] Ballast water / VGP / BWTS — With overdue BWTS extension letter or AMS-BWTS, ocean exchange is NOT allowed (heavy fines). VGP and BFMP to be maintained per Docmap US documentation; Ballast Water Logbook per Circular 025-19.

[General] RACE drill & response plans — RACE drill compliance per CFR (one fleet vessel per 3 years); NTVRP & CANTVCP to be kept updated; QI notification drill required — any serious accident in USA/Canada reported to QI.

[Security] US port security advisory — Vessels that visited countries listed in the USCG Port Security Advisory during their last five port calls must take prescribed actions 1-5 as a condition of entry into US ports.
[General] CBP visa penalty — Approx. USD 6,000 per person imposed when crew without valid US visa go out via stern ramp. Strict access control required.

[General] Bunkering & NOA — Annual hydrostatic testing of bunker lines per CFR 156. Do NOT sign bunkering agreements indemnifying the barge under OPA. Fuel type must be indicated on NOA per USCG MSIB-11-23.

[General] EEXI / EPL (USCG Policy Letter 01-24) — Pilot Card updated with original/limited RPM & power; override & recording procedure posted at bridge and ECR consoles; officers familiarized; report to Class/OCMI if override activated.
[General] AGM certification — USA is an AGM country (with Canada, Chile, Argentina, Australia, NZ); crew pre-inspection and AGM certificate obtained before departure from Asia.

[General] CARB fuel & MISP — Only low-sulphur distillate (S<0.1%) accepted; EGCS/scrubber compliance not allowed (CARB Marine Notice 2020-1). Register at misp.io for annual & ballast reports; Biofouling Management Plan updated and paint certificate onboard for Marine Invasive Species inspection.
[General] TWIC shore access — Shore leave requires TWIC compliance; obtain arrangements from local agent, especially at Charleston. Crew must confirm with Master before going ashore.

[General] COFR bridging letter — For Brunswick, New York and US East Coast calls a bridging letter is required; verify COFR at npfc.uscg.mil/cofr. Georgia whale-speed reporting also applies (1 May - 15 Dec).
[General] COFR bridging letter — Bridging letter required for New York / East Coast calls; check COFR status at npfc.uscg.mil/cofr before arrival.
[General] Whale speed limit (TSS) — Voluntary participation in San Francisco TSS whale speed restrictions; feed into passage plan and comply during 1 May - 15 Dec.
[General] 1-Call Alaska & Aleutian ATBA — Notify the 1-Call Alaska provider when transiting; IMO Aleutian Areas To Be Avoided marked on ECDIS, inform 1-Call if entry needed.
[General] IMO Area To Be Avoided off the Washington Coast — reflect in passage plan and keep clear.
[General] Oil-spill response agreements — WCMRC (West) / ECRC (East) agreements required for Canadian calls incl. New Westminster and Tacoma; ERTV & Juan de Fuca Agreement applicable.

[General] Whale slowdown & navigation limits — Voluntary slowdown at Swiftsure Bank (Jun-Oct) and Haro Strait/Boundary Pass (Jun-Nov), No-Go Zone at San Juan Island. Canada is an AGM country. Check H&M navigation limits and SSMM 7.33 ice/cold-weather precautions.

[General] PCSOPEP — Plan approval required (submit 96h before; USD 2,000 penalty for non-compliance); Authorized-Person notification exercise twice per year documented for ACP verification. Minimum transit draft and Panama light fuel to be reviewed.

[General] Transit equipment requirements — Wheelhouse/pilot A/C must hold 21-26 C and 40-70% RH or disruption charge applies (OP Notice N-1-2023 s.24). Green Vessel Classification: IEEC/EEDI, bow-thruster/displacement ratio and BDN submitted. NPU/PPU fixed RTK antenna procedure applies.
[General] Terminal access — Walking or cycling inside Zeebrugge terminal is prohibited; crew must contact the agency for arranged transport to/from the gate.

[General] Freshwater analysis & wastewater — Arrange freshwater analysis (galley, purifier, cabins; 3-6 month interval) before arrival. Port guidelines on vessel wastewater and in-water hull cleaning to be reviewed.
[General] HIT berth access — At Humber International Terminal the ship's ramp/gangway may become unusable at low tide; arrange the shore gangway via local agent or HIT to keep safe access.

[General] Shore access & heaving lines — Crew walking to town must use designated walkways wearing Hi-Viz vests. Monkey fist must be <500 g without added weights (penalties imposed at Southampton and Amsterdam).
[General] Compulsory garbage/sludge collection — Per EU directive a constant collection fee for garbage and sludge/bilge applies to all vessels calling Piraeus; discharge per port regulation.

[General] KIA Terminal / PIRT — Transshipment of unlashed vehicles between KIA Terminal & PIRT per WW instruction INF-12-23. KIA Terminal prohibits shore vehicles >7 t (affects lube-oil supply; plan LO stems in advance).

[General] Korea ECA & domestic requirements — 0.1%S fuel at Incheon, Pyeongtaek-Dangjin, Yeosu-Gwangyang, Busan and Ulsan (from 1h after berthing/anchoring until 1h before departure). While drifting, engine kept ready and proper lights shown. VHF recording (Korea flag/BBCHP), KCG inspections, MLC complaint procedure displayed, ballast reporting to agent.

[General] Fishing nets & territorial sea — Check set-nets on the route with local agent before arrival. Foreign ships must not navigate Japanese territorial sea (3NM) / internal waters with restricted actions except emergencies.

[General] Mooring & pilot boarding — Mooring winch brake rendering test at intervals not exceeding 24 months (rules effective 1 Feb 2023). Strict pilot boarding arrangement: photos submitted with 48h NOA; non-compliance cancels the schedule until rectification.
[General] Expanded VTS area — Port of Melbourne VTS area expanded (Victorian NtM 127/2023); comply with VTS reporting and general traffic procedures.

[General] Reef navigation & Queensland pilotage — Penalties imposed for improper navigation in the Great Barrier Reef. Queensland pilotage: EPL/ShaPoLi must be immediately overridable; fuel changeover completed and propulsion tested 2h before pilot boarding (30 min from berth); no changeover under pilotage.
[General] Pilot boarding safety — Ports of Auckland safety update: risk of improperly secured pilot ladders; verify rigging and securing before pilot transfer.

[General] Biofouling (CRMS) & entry — Clean hull required per Craft Risk Management Standard; follow MPI 5 steps (inspection, reports, paperwork, delay notice, pre-departure advice). Poor Knights Islands exclusion zone must be avoided (MSA fine). All seafarers require valid AU/NZ visas.

[Security] Stowaway regulation — Stowaways boarding at Durban will not be landed back: if deemed stowaways they sail with the vessel to the next port. Heightened stowaway watch and pre-departure searches required.

[General] Blue-whale routing (WalWil fleet) — Company TSS moved ~15NM south of the current TSS to avoid whale feeding grounds: westbound 05 30N-05 35N, eastbound 05 24N-05 29N. Reflect in passage plan.
